summary: Earth System Trend Detective is a free web tool that helps students and the public find out what is changing on Earth, where, by how much, and whether the change is real. Users pick a variable (temperature, rainfall, humidity, sunlight or wind), a place on the map, and a season. The tool pulls NASA POWER monthly data, which is built from NASA satellite observations and the MERRA-2 model, plots the time series, fits a trend line, and tests significance with the Mann-Kendall test and a t-test. A "detective scan" checks all five variables at once to show which ones are trending. A compare mode puts two places side by side to show that the same planet can change differently in different regions. Plain-English verdicts, variable definitions and year-by-year color stripes make the science easy to read. It matters because climate change is regional, and people need a simple way to tell real trends from noise.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Earth System Trend Detective lets anyone investigate whether an Earth science variable is changing over time. The user chooses a variable (air temperature, rainfall, relative humidity, surface sunlight, wind speed), a location (map click, city search, or coordinates), a time period (1981-2025), and a season. The tool then shows what is changing, where, how much, and whether the change is statistically significant.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Monthly data for the chosen location comes from the NASA POWER API.

2. Values are averaged by year (or by the chosen season). Yearly averaging removes the seasonal cycle so it does not hide the trend.

3. A linear trend is fitted, giving the rate of change per decade with a 95% confidence range.

4. Significance is tested two ways: a t-test on the slope, and the Mann-Kendall test, which does not assume normally distributed data. Sen's slope gives an outlier-resistant rate. A trend with Mann-Kendall p < 0.05 is called significant.

5. Results are shown as a plain-English verdict, a chart, year-by-year stripes, and a statistics panel.

KEY FEATURES

- Detective scan: tests all five variables at the chosen place and ranks which ones show significant trends, which helps users decide what to investigate.

- Compare mode: puts two places side by side, showing that trends can differ by region.

- Season selector for winter, spring, summer or autumn trends.

- Variable definitions and plain-language explanations for students and the public.

- Six built-in demo cases, CSV download, and a shareable link for any investigation.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

The tool makes trend analysis of NASA data usable without any coding or statistics background. It teaches users to tell a real trend from natural year-to-year variation, and that "not significant" is still a meaningful finding.

TOOLS

HTML, CSS and JavaScript (single page, no backend), Chart.js for charts, Leaflet with CARTO/OpenStreetMap for the map, Nominatim for place search, hosted on Netlify.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED AND LIMITS

The tool detects straight-line trends only. A significant trend shows that something changed, not why. The data is a model-and-satellite blend for a grid cell of about 50 km, not a weather station. Longer periods (20+ years) give more reliable results.

SI USE

The code and the text of this project were written with the help of Claude, a large language model made by Anthropic.
